question: As part of the EU Biodiversity Strategy 2030, Member States pledge to protect 30 % of the EU’s land and 30 % of its marine areas by 2030, of which 10 % must be strictly protected. In this regard, it was expected that Member States would submit their individual pledges and thus their contribution to the 30 % protection objective, as outlined in the strategy, before the end of 2023.

As the European Commission mentioned in its answer to question E-003201/2023, up until the date of the answer (15/12/2023), only five of the twenty seven Member States had submitted their pledges regarding protected areas. 1.
Could the European Commission clarify which other Member States have submitted their pledges since then?
What is the Commission planning to do in the event that Member States do not submit their pledges?
Based on the pledges that have already been submitted, does the Commission consider that the EU is on the right track to reach its protection objectives by 2030?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.5.2024) 1. So far, six Member States have submitted pledges for the protected area targets in the EU Biodiversity Strategy for 20301: Denmark, France, Germany, Luxembourg, Spain and Sweden. 2. Submitting pledges is not a pre-condition for achieving progress in terms of protected area designations.

The Commission intends to continue the dialogue with Member States and to review the pledges through biogeographical seminars and other relevant events, with a view to supporting the achievement of the protected area targets by 2030 and keeping track of progress in terms of protected area designations.

Furthermore, the Commission is continuously working to ensure the completion of the Natura 2000 network through bilateral nature dialogues. It is also taking enforcement action when necessary to ensure the full implementation of the Birds2 and Habitats3 Directives. 3.
Due to the limited number of pledges received so far, the Commission does not have enough information to assess whether the EU is on track to reach its protected area objectives by 2030.
1 https://environment.ec.europa.eu/strategy/biodiversity-strategy-2030_en 2 Directive 2009/147/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 30 November 2009 on the

conservation of wild birds, OJ L 20, 26.1.2010, p. 7–25. 3 Council Directive 92/43/EEC of 21 May 1992 on the conservation of natural habitats and of wild fauna and flora, OJ L 206, 22.7.1992, p. 7–50.
